Kimi K3 cooked Opus 5, GPT-5.6, and Claude Fable 5 in my opinion. 

Someone had Opus 5 generate this game from a single prompt.

Then gave GPT-5.6 Sol nothing but the gameplay video and asked it to recreate the experience.

The result was impressive.

GPT-5.6 Sol produced a fast, well-optimized prototype that captured much of the gameplay.

But Opus 5 still came out ahead in the areas that make a game feel believable: world composition, environmental detail, camera direction, atmosphere, and overall 3D scene coherence.

It’s becoming clear that raw code generation is only part of the story. Design judgment is starting to matter just as much.

items.title: THE NEW RASPBERRY PI AI HAT DOES SOMETHING THE OLD $70 ONE COULDN'T: RUN A REAL LANGUAGE MODEL, NOT JUST DETECT OBJECTS.
items.summary:
THE NEW RASPBERRY PI AI HAT DOES SOMETHING THE OLD $70 ONE COULDN'T: RUN A REAL LANGUAGE MODEL, NOT JUST DETECT OBJECTS.

that clip is the new hailo ai hat sitting on a raspberry pi 5.

it looks almost identical to the old one. the whole jump is inside.

here's the ladder, verified:

the original $70 ai kit was a hailo-8l, 13 tops. brilliant at vision - object detection, pose, segmentation - but no generative ai at all

the ai hat+ steps up to 26 tops on a hailo-8, chip soldered to the board for better cooling, still vision-first

the new ai hat+ 2 is the real leap: a hailo-10h, 40 tops, with 8gb of its own memory, for around $130

that onboard memory is the reason it finally runs small language models and vision-language models on the device itself - not just drawing boxes around cars

so the upgrade isn't "faster detection." it's a category change.

the pi went from a thing that watches to a thing that reads and answers, fully offline.

pair it with a pi 5 and 16gb of ram, and a stack around $250 detects objects in real time and holds a small local chat - no cloud, no api key, no data leaving the desk.

it's still a tiny model. don't expect gpt on a pi.

but "it runs a real llm on a raspberry pi" is a sentence you couldn't say a year ago.

no cloud subscription, no vision-only ceiling, no data leaving the house.

follow @RetroChainer for more of the small boxes doing big things, and bookmark this one so you can find it again.

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development' - Business Insider
items.summary: # Over 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development'. "We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." items.title: Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and e
items.summary:
Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and every account you have ever blown.

MIT put the entire course online. it has been free for over twenty years. almost nobody finishes it.

His point: the market never pays in certainties. it pays in probabilities, and a human gut can barely hold one straight. the math that holds ten thousand at once, weighs them, and collapses them into a single call is linear algebra. it is the branch Citadel and OpenAI both pay $400K to hire for.

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

Skip to where he turns a wall of numbers into one vector. a single object carrying a thousand odds at once, in notation a beginner can follow.

No slides. no jargon. one piece of chalk.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

items.title: 10 agent evals every AI engineer should know
items.summary:
10 agent evals every AI engineer should know

1) golden set

a frozen set of cases you run after every prompt model or tool change

use it as your baseline to see whether the system improved or quietly broke

OpenAI Evals helps you build repeatable benchmark sets and compare model changes

→ https://t.co/dr1GZlC75R

2) llm as judge

a second model scores open ended answers against a written rubric

use it when there is no exact output to compare against

OpenEvals provides ready made evaluators for LLM applications

→ https://t.co/S2yhnByFIP

3) rubric scoring

score correctness tone safety and cost separately

one quality number hides the problem

DeepEval helps you create custom metrics and score every dimension independently

→ https://t.co/q9Z6Xmixia

4) trajectory eval

grade the path the agent took

not only the final answer

AgentEvals checks agent actions decisions and tool calls across the full trajectory

→ https://t.co/0oziAl54az

5) tool unit tests

test every tool with fixed inputs and outputs

no model in the loop

MCP Inspector helps you inspect and test MCP servers tools and responses separately

→ https://t.co/IVmt5qpWIN

6) regression suite

replay previous runs against every new prompt model or toolset

then compare the results

Promptfoo helps you run repeatable eval suites catch regressions and add checks to CI

→ https://t.co/zxi2PuWuhe

7) a b in prod

split real traffic between two versions and compare actual outcomes

GrowthBook provides feature flags controlled experiments and product analytics

→ https://t.co/DGlE3JjDD3

8) human review

sample real runs and let a person grade them honestly

use it to calibrate your automated judge

Argilla helps teams collect human feedback review outputs and build better datasets

→ https://t.co/QHWb7skWjr

9) shadow run

let the candidate run on real traffic while its output is shown to nobody

use it before a risky rollout

Langfuse helps you trace production runs compare candidates and monitor eval results

→ https://t.co/IrhDf38tRn

10) red team

attack the system before somebody else does

jailbreaks prompt injection data leaks and tool abuse

Garak scans LLM systems for vulnerabilities and unsafe behavior

→ https://t.co/w8ObyW4ZKv

offline evals tell you it works

online evals tell you it still works

you probably do not need all ten today

start with the two that would have caught your last outage

bookmark this

・そのvaultをClaude Codeで開いて、Karpathyの設計メモ（wikiのアイデアを書いた1枚）を渡して「これ作って」と言う

・AIが箱を3つ用意する（raw＝素材用／wiki＝AIが整えたページ用／CLAUDE. md＝動かすルール1枚）

・rawに素材（記事・PDF・文字起こし）を放り込んで「取り込んで」と言う

・あとは全部を横断して、いつでも聞ける

セットアップは5分。これで、白紙のチャットから毎回始めなくてよくなる。

なんでまだみんなこれを使ってないのか、本気で分からない。

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development' - Business Insider
items.summary: # Over 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development'. Senior officials at some of the nation's leading AI companies say it's time for the federal government to find a way to put the brakes on AI development if it's needed. "We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." Anthropic has shared that its Claude models are quickly approaching that threshold. Look out for an alert in your inbox the next time a new story is published!

Healthcare robotics faces critical challenges in data scarcity, generalization, and development velocity due to limited access to annotated demonstrations, the prevalence of rare but clinically important scenarios, and slow, resource-intensive prototyping cycles. [...] AI-generated content may summarize information incompletely. Verify important information. Learn more

Unlike autonomous driving or industrial robotics, healthcare robotics can’t rely on internet-scale data collection or unlimited real-world experimentation. Every demonstration requires specialized equipment, clinical expertise, and access to patients or laboratory environments. This creates three fundamental challenges for developers. [...] The third challenge is development velocity. Medical robotics development relies on benchtop phantoms, cadaver studies, animal models, and limited clinical evaluations. These remain essential, but they are inherently sequential, expensive, and difficult to scale. Iterating on designs and algorithms currently takes months, pushing total development cycles to 4–7 years.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary:
OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place. [...] # What happened?

On July 16, Hugging Face said it had been hit by an unusually automated cyberattack. Over the course of a weekend, AI agents carried out thousands of actions across many temporary virtual computers, moving through the company’s internal systems and shifting the infrastructure coordinating the attack between online services to keep it running. Five days later, OpenAI disclosed that its own models were responsible.
